source.proofTitle: Green's Theorem: Minimal Regularity (Lipschitz Curves and L¹ Curl)

knowledge.progressSummary: DECIDE (build-gated): Sessions 1/3 reduced the OQ to one missing keystone — the function-level FTC-for-absolutely-continuous bridge `f b - f a = ∫ x in a..b, deriv f x` from an a.e./L¹ derivative — and Session 3 began building it manually (a StatementOnly Lipschitz-FTC Aristotle target). builtItems: Authored proofs/Proofs/StatementOnly_GreensOQ02_FTCofLipschitz.lean — one-theorem Aristotle batch target (ftc_of_lipschitzOn) with informal block + Rivin scaffolding. UNVERIFIED (Docker down): compile-check + batch submission pending infra restore.
insights: The `greens_theorem_l1curl` axiom (GreensTheoremOQ02.lean:350) is stated over a RECTANGLE domain `Set.Icc a b ×ˢ Set.Icc c d` with the curve C a Lipschitz parametrization of its frontier (hTraversal). The geometric domain is therefore SIMPLE — so the axiom docstring's cited requirement of 'sets of finite perimeter, Federer's trace theorem, Gauss-Green formula' is an overstatement for THIS case. Those are needed for general Lipschitz DOMAINS, not for a rectangle with a Lipschitz boundary parametrization.

The genuine gap vs the axiom-free OQ01 (GreensTheoremOQ01.lean, 0 axioms, uses pointwise `HasDerivAt` + `intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt`) is exactly the weakening of the hypothesis from pointwise-C¹ partial derivatives to an a.e. curl formula with merely L¹-integrable curl (hCurlAE + hL1). Via Fubini (`MeasureTheory.integral_prod`) the rectangle double integral splits into iterated 1D integrals, each of which needs FTC for a function whose derivative is only L¹/a.e.-defined — i.e. FTC for absolutely continuous functions.

Mathlib's FTC (`Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.FundThmCalculus`) provides ONLY versions requiring continuity at the endpoints or `HasDerivAt`/`HasDerivWithinAt` on the whole interval. It does NOT provide the Lebesgue/AC direction `f absolutely continuous ⟹ f b - f a = ∫_a^b f'` from an a.e. L¹ derivative. This is the keystone the OQ02 axiom needs (confirmed via mathlib4_docs FundThmCalculus + arXiv 2509.05247 survey of the FTC-for-Lebesgue result).

Mathlib DOES have the supporting ingredients the OQ names: `Mathlib.Analysis.BoundedVariation` (eVariationOn, `LipschitzWith.boundedVariationOn`, BV ⟹ a.e. differentiable), Rademacher (`Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Rademacher`, Lipschitz ⟹ a.e. differentiable), and measure-level `MeasureTheory.Measure.AbsolutelyContinuous` (μ ≪ ν) + Radon-Nikodym (`Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Decomposition.RadonNikodym`). NOTE: `Measure.AbsolutelyContinuous` is AC of MEASURES, not of functions — the OQ's intended path is to model the L¹ curl as the RN-derivative of an AC measure and recover boundary values, which still bottlenecks on the same function-level FTC bridge.

Answer to the OQ as stated: PARTIALLY / not directly. The named BoundedVariation + Measure.AbsolutelyContinuous API is the correct toolkit but is insufficient on its own; the dischargeability hinges entirely on building the FTC-for-AC bridge lemma, after which the rectangle case follows by Fubini + the existing OQ01-style boundary algebra.

Session 3 (2026-06-14): refined the keystone gap to its cleanest tractable first building block — FTC for Lipschitz functions: LipschitzOnWith on [a,b] ⟹ f b - f a = ∫ x in a..b, deriv f x. This is statable in plain Mathlib (no AbsolutelyContinuous-of-functions predicate needed) and captures the hard AC⟹FTC content; rectangle boundary edges are themselves Lipschitz.

True obstruction localized: integral_eq_sub_of_hasDeriv_right_of_le needs an everywhere right-derivative on (a,b); Lipschitz/Rademacher only gives it a.e., so the AC theory bridging a.e.-derivative to FTC is exactly the missing piece.
Aristotle MCP server is currently DOWN (prove() returns "Resource not found") — the server-side proving avenue is unavailable this session alongside the Docker blackout.

Session 4 (2026-06-14): the keystone is NO LONGER a Mathlib gap — it was added UPSTREAM. `AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval.integral_deriv_eq_sub {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} (hf : AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval f a b) : ∫ (x : ℝ) in a..b, deriv f x = f b - f a` lives in Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/IntervalIntegral/AbsolutelyContinuousFun.lean, together with integration-by-parts `integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul`. Introduced by PR #29508 (Yizheng Zhu, merged 2026-02-02, part of #29092). Verified via GitHub API that the file is ABSENT at the repo's pinned v4.26.0 (2025-12-13) and PRESENT from v4.28.0 (2026-02-16) onward. This is the GENERAL AC version, strictly stronger than Session 3's Lipschitz-only `ftc_of_lipschitzOn` target — so the StatementOnly Aristotle artifact is superseded (kept only as a no-bump fallback).

Session 4 discharge wiring (build-gated): the OQ02 hypotheses give the curl a.e. (hCurlAE) + L¹ integrability (hL1), not 'P,Q are AC'. Bridge: write each 1D rectangle slice (e.g. x ↦ Q(x,y)) as `c + ∫_a^x (∂Q/∂x)`, which is AC by `IntervalIntegrable.absolutelyContinuousOnInterval_intervalIntegral` (also in v4.28.0), then apply `integral_deriv_eq_sub`. Combine the two slice directions via Fubini (`MeasureTheory.integral_prod`) over the rectangle and reuse OQ01's boundary algebra. The AC-function predicate `AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval` + its algebra (add/sub/mul/const_smul) and supporting lemmas (intervalIntegrable_deriv, ae_differentiableAt) are all present at v4.28.0.
mathlibGaps: RESOLVED UPSTREAM (v4.28.0): The function-level FTC for absolutely continuous functions — once the keystone gap — now exists as `AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval.integral_deriv_eq_sub` in Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/IntervalIntegral/AbsolutelyContinuousFun.lean (PR #29508). It is ABSENT at the repo's pinned v4.26.0 and PRESENT from v4.28.0 onward. The repo must bump its Mathlib pin (>= v4.28.0) to use it. NOTE: FTC itself moved to Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral.FundThmCalculus in recent Mathlib.

NO LONGER A GAP (v4.28.0): the bridge identifying an AC function's a.e. derivative with the FTC integrand is packaged via `IntervalIntegrable.absolutelyContinuousOnInterval_intervalIntegral` (the integral of an L¹ function is AC) used inside the upstream proof. The remaining repo-side work is purely the Mathlib version bump + the rectangle Fubini reduction (no foundational measure theory left to build).

Discharge `greens_theorem_l1curl`: import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral.AbsolutelyContinuousFun; Fubini-split the rectangle integral (MeasureTheory.integral_prod); for each 1D slice write it as `c + ∫_a^x partial`, get AC via IntervalIntegrable.absolutelyContinuousOnInterval_intervalIntegral, apply integral_deriv_eq_sub, match the a.e. partial via hCurlAE; assemble the line-integral side with OQ01's boundary algebra. Then flip the `axiom` to a proved `theorem` and update axiomCount in the gallery meta + this JSON.

Sanity check before claiming discharge: the reduction must recover OQ01's conclusion when the curl comes from genuine `HasDerivAt` partials (C¹ ⟹ L¹ on compact rectangle), matching the existing `greens_oq1_from_l1curl` theorem already in GreensTheoremOQ02.lean.
